  title = {Blanked-out optional fields in training are measured under a rule fixed before the first fit},
  date = {2026-10-13},

  participants = {@kadameit proposed it (\href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/issues/116}{issue \#116}); @lukas2510 decided to measure it and left the protocol to the AI},
  decision = {We measure whether training \texttt{lgbm-\allowbreak{}extended} on copies of the listings with optional fields blanked out removes its collapse on sparse requests, which is why \texttt{lgbm-\allowbreak{}basic} is the candidate (\hyperref[EDN-62]{EDN-62}).
The configurations, the scenarios and the rule a configuration has to meet were committed before the first fit, and the test split is not read.},
  rationale = {\emph{Alternatives considered:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt]
\item \textbf{Option A (measured): train with blanked-out fields.}
One model for every request, and the UC2 interval models need the same masking; it multiplies the training rows and may cost accuracy on complete requests.
\item \textbf{Option B: serve both models, routed by how full a request is.}
Never worse than either model, but two models in the image and a threshold to explain.
\item \textbf{Option C: keep \texttt{lgbm-\allowbreak{}basic} without measuring.}
No work, but the project brief's open question on masking stays open.
\end{itemize}
\par
\emph{Why:} Single optional fields are empty in 1\,\% to 95\,\% of the 60,378 training rows, but all 23 are empty together in only 5, so a request with only the required fields lies outside what the model saw, and blanked copies put it inside.
A configuration qualifies only if it passes SC-06, is not measurably worse than \texttt{lgbm-\allowbreak{}basic} on the required-only request and is measurably better on the complete one, on the validation split, by the paired bootstrap of \hyperref[EDN-73]{EDN-73}.
The result and what follows from it are added here once measured.},
